newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gov't bills dip in line with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: HK gov't bills dip in line with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Hong Kong government bills were priced slightly lower on Wednesday in line with the dip in demand for U.S. Treasuries overnight, dealers said.

Yields of seven-year Exchange Fund notes were pushed up to 7.36 percent versus 7.30 on Tuesday, five-year notes ended at 7.02 percent against 6.96, and three-year notes were little changed at 6.48 percent versus 6.37.
The one-week Exchange Fund bill closed at 4.78 percent versus 4.80 percent.
"For longer term bills, demand has fallen but just in line with the U.S. overnight," a dealer with an American bank said.
On the interbank market, rates were little changed as participants stayed at the sidelines waiting for the release of the U.S. producer price index (PPI) on Friday, dealers said.
The overnight ended unchanged at 5-1/8 percent while three month money finished at 5-1/2 7/16 percent versus 5-1/2 percent.
